`compute_delta()` (in `rdf/delta.py`) classifies the difference between two PSGC snapshots into a
fixed set of canonical event types, emitted as `psgc:event/...` URIs (see [URIs](uris.qmd)).

## Canonical event types

The authoritative set is the `ChangeEvent.event_type` enum in `models/schemas.py` (10 types).
`compute_delta()` actually **emits** these seven:

- `creation` — a new entity appears in the later snapshot.
- `deletion` — an entity disappears.
- `code_change` — identity preserved (same correspondence code), but the 10-digit PSGC code changed.
- `renaming` — name change, same identity.
- `merger` — two or more entities combine into one.
- `split` — one entity divides into two or more.
- `transfer` — an entity moves to a different parent unit.

The remaining three enum values — `reclassification`, `reenlistment`, and `unknown` — are modelled
by the schema and accepted by the parser/RDF builder, but are not currently produced by
`compute_delta()` (reclassifications, for example, surface as a `creation`+`deletion` pair today).

## Per-type triple shape

Every event is an `org:ChangeEvent` with a `dct:date` (the snapshot date), a `dct:description`, and
an `org:classification` link to a `psgc:concept/change-type/{type}` concept. The difference between
types is **which organization links** they carry:

| Type | `org:originalOrganization` | `org:resultingOrganization` | Meaning |
|------|:---:|:---:|---------|
| `creation` | — | ✓ (1) | new entity appears |
| `deletion` | ✓ (1) | — | entity disappears |
| `code_change` | ✓ (1) | ✓ (1) | same identity, new 10-digit PSGC code |
| `renaming` | ✓ (1) | ✓ (1) | name change, identity preserved |
| `merger` | ✓ (n) | ✓ (1) | several entities combine into one |
| `split` | ✓ (1) | ✓ (n) | one entity divides into several |
| `transfer` | ✓ (1) | ✓ (1) | entity moves to a different parent |

Worked examples of these links are in [Entity & event URIs](uris.qmd).

Each committed delta carries the legal basis for its events via `dct:source`, the effective date via
`prov:generatedAtTime`, and a human-readable summary via `dct:description`.
